incidents.label: Al Taqaddum object report, October 2017
incidents.description: AARO and DVIDS report that infrared footage from an aerostat near Al Taqaddum Air Base showed an unidentified object. The video itself was not independently inspected for this dataset.

claims.assertionText: On October 23, 2017, an infrared (IR) sensor aboard an aerostat force protection dirigible (blimp) operating at 2,700 feet above Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, recorded 17 minutes and 30 seconds of footage featuring an unidentified object that appears to be floating above the ground.

sourceLocator.description: PDF page 1, Case Overview, opening paragraph.

claims.assertionText: AARO assesses with high confidence that the object was consistent with a cluster of fully and partially inflated balloons (Figure 1).

sourceLocator.description: PDF page 1, AARO Assessment and Case Status.

locator.description: PDF page 1, AARO Assessment and Case Status.

claims.assertionText: AARO assesses with high confidence that the Al Taqaddum object did not exhibit anomalous behavior or capabilities.

sourceLocator.description: PDF page 1, AARO Assessment and Case Status.

locator.description: PDF page 1, AARO Assessment and Case Status.

claims.assertionText: AARO based this assessment on analysis of full-motion video, video metadata, line-of-sight, scenario reconstructions, and weather data analysis.

sourceLocator.description: PDF page 1, paragraph following AARO Assessment and Case Status.

claims.assertionText: Figure 1: Stills of the UAP from the 17-minute video. Aerostat deployed at Al Taqaddum Air Base. The balloons appear as bulbous, rounded shapes; similarly, the strings and deflated balloons can be seen hanging below. These images were assigned different color temperatures to aid in visualization.
The DVIDS page displays the literal Date Taken value “10.01.2017”.
In October 2017, an infrared sensor onboard a force protection aerostat near Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, captured 17 minutes of video of an unidentified object.

sourceLocator.text: In October 2017, an infrared sensor onboard a force protection aerostat near Al Taqaddum Air Base, Iraq, captured 17 minutes of video of an unidentified object.

claims.assertionText: The DVIDS page lists the video Length as “00:17:27”.

AARO assesses that the object was a cluster of partially and fully inflated balloons. The object's appearance is consistent with other recorded observations featuring balloon clusters. AARO employed full-motion video analysis and pixel examination techniques to inform its assessment.

relationshipNotes.basis: Inferred from matching descriptions: AARO says its assessment used full-motion video and describes Figure 1 as stills from the 17-minute Al Taqaddum video; DVIDS describes an October 2017 infrared-aerostat recording at Al Taqaddum and lists video ID 960331. The inspected AARO report does not explicitly identify the DVIDS URL or video ID. This is not an independent confirmation.
The DVIDS page explicitly attributes this assessment to AARO. The DVIDS page text is not an independent corroboration of the underlying assessment.

discrepancies.description: AARO identifies the event date as 23 October 2017. DVIDS displays the literal Date Taken value 10.01.2017. The notation and meaning of the DVIDS field have not been established here; the difference is unresolved and is not silently interpreted as a confirmed event date.

AARO's Case Overview says 17 minutes and 30 seconds; DVIDS lists Length as 00:17:27. DVIDS also describes the recording as 17 minutes in its opening text. The exact difference between the stated and listed durations is preserved without assuming an explanation.
